title: CHAPTER 4: ECONOMIC GROWTH AND ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT

blocks.content: This chapter explains the difference between Economic Growth and Economic Development in the deepest possible manner for SSC examinations. Many students confuse growth with development. Hence, each concept is explained step-by-step with definitions, characteristics, indicators, examples and formulas wherever required.
PART A: ECONOMIC GROWTH (IN FULL DEPTH)

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Economic Growth refers to a quantitative increase in a country's real national output or per capita income over time.
Economic Development is a broader, qualitative concept encompassing economic growth alongside structural changes, poverty reduction, and improved living standards.
Primary indicators of economic development include Per Capita Income, Health Indicators, Education Indicators, and Employment Indicators.
The Human Development Index (HDI) measures progress across three essential dimensions: Long and healthy life, Knowledge, and Decent standard of living.
Sustainable Development focuses on fulfilling the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs.

blocks.content: 1. Meaning of Economic Growth
Economic Growth refers to a sustained increase in the real output or real national income of a country over a period of time. It indicates an expansion in the productive capacity of an economy.
Economic Growth is a quantitative concept because it is measured numerically. It focuses mainly on the increase in income and production.
2. Measurement of Economic Growth
Economic Growth is measured using Real GDP or Real National Income, because real values remove the effect of inflation.

Formula:

Economic Growth Rate (%) = [(Real GDP in current year − Real GDP in previous year) / Real GDP in previous year] × 100
3. Features of Economic Growth

• Quantitative in nature

• Measured using real income

• Focuses on production and output

• Does not directly measure welfare

• Can occur without improvement in quality of life
4. Limitations of Economic Growth
Economic Growth does not show income distribution, poverty, unemployment, health, education or environmental quality. Hence, growth alone is not sufficient for overall progress.
PART B: ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT
5. Meaning of Economic Development

Economic Development refers to a long-term process in which there is improvement in the standard of living of people. It includes growth in income as well as reduction in poverty, inequality and unemployment.
Economic Development is both a quantitative and qualitative concept. It focuses on human welfare, not just income.
6. Features of Economic Development
CHAPTER 4: ECONOMIC GROWTH AND ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT

• Includes economic growth

• Improves quality of life

• Reduces poverty and inequality

• Improves health and education

• Long-term and continuous process
7. Objectives of Economic Development

The main objectives of economic development are:

• Increase in per capita income

• Reduction of poverty

• Full employment

• Social justice and equality

• Sustainable use of resources
PART C: DIFFERENCE BETWEEN ECONOMIC GROWTH AND ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT

Economic Growth refers only to increase in output or income, whereas Economic Development refers to overall improvement in human well-being. Growth can take place without development, but development cannot occur without growth.
PART D: INDICATORS OF ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT
8. Per Capita Income
Per Capita Income is calculated by dividing National Income by total population. It gives the average income of citizens.

Formula:

Per Capita Income = National Income / Total Population

rows: Broad (focuses on health, education, living standards)
Measured by Real GDP, Real GNP, Per Capita Income
Measured by HDI, PQLI, health & literacy rates

blocks.content: 9. Health Indicators
Health indicators include life expectancy at birth, infant mortality rate, maternal mortality rate and access to healthcare services.
10. Education Indicators
Education indicators include literacy rate, enrolment ratio and years of schooling.
11. Employment Indicators
High employment and productive employment indicate better economic development.
PART E: HUMAN DEVELOPMENT INDEX (HDI – FULL COVERAGE)
12. Meaning of HDI
Human Development Index is a composite index published by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP). It measures development using three basic dimensions.
13. Components of HDI

• Health – Life expectancy at birth

• Education – Mean years of schooling and expected years of schooling

• Income – Gross National Income per capita (PPP)
14. Importance of HDI

items: Economic Growth is strictly quantitative (measured via GDP/PCI), whereas Economic Development includes both quantitative and qualitative structural changes.
HDI consists of 3 dimensions (Health, Education, Standard of Living) measured using 4 specific indicators.
Questions frequently test the core definition of Sustainable Development regarding inter-generational equity.

blocks.content: HDI provides a more comprehensive measure of development than income alone. It highlights human welfare.
PART F: SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT
15. Meaning of Sustainable Development
Sustainable Development means development that meets present needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their needs.
16. Need for Sustainable Development
It ensures environmental protection, efficient resource use and long-term growth.
SSC HYPER FINAL REVISION POINTS

• Economic Growth = increase in real income

• Economic Development = growth + welfare

• Growth is quantitative, development is qualitative

• HDI measures human development

• Sustainable development protects future generations
